title: radial mean
semantics: Edges point to prerequisites; dependencies are conjunctive; one alternative route suffices. Reviewed source topology, not a kernel proof trace.
conventions: Carriers, hypotheses, quantifiers and constant scope are recorded per node and in the corresponding Lean declarations.

nodes.title: Defining formula of the mean for r > 0

edges.rationale: the r > 0 branch of the defined f̄ is exactly the displayed formula (3.7)

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞) ; r > 0
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞), for all r > 0

nodes.title: Radial mean f̄(r) = r⁻¹∫₀^r f, with centre value f(0)
nodes.source_hypotheses: f is one fixed-u slice of a function of (u,r), regarded as a continuous real function of r on [0,∞) (, ; domain 0 ≤ r < ∞ from p. 339)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for each continuous f on [0,∞) and each r in [0,∞)
nodes.source_conclusion: f̄(r) := (1/r)∫₀^r f(r')dr' for r > 0, and f̄(0) := f(0) (centre value, p. 344, )

nodes.title: First identity of (3.8): ∂_r(r f̄) = f

edges.rationale: the identity concerns r f̄ for the defined f̄
the derivative of r ↦ ∫₀^r f within [0,∞) is f(r)
on [0,∞), r f̄ coincides with r ↦ ∫₀^r f, so the within-[0,∞) derivative transfers

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞), for all r in [0,∞)
nodes.source_conclusion: r ↦ r f̄(r) has derivative f(r) at r within [0,∞) (one-sided from the right at r = 0, )

nodes.title: FTC for r ↦ ∫₀^r f (one-sided at 0)

edges.rationale: supplies the integrability premise of the FTC
FTC at a point of continuity of the integrand, one-sided at the endpoint 0

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞), for all r ≥ 0
nodes.source_conclusion: G(r) := ∫₀^r f has derivative f(r) at r within [0,∞) (right-sided at r = 0)

nodes.title: The integrand s ↦ f(s) is interval-integrable on [0,r]

edges.rationale: a continuous integrand on a compact interval is integrable, so the integral in (3.7) is a genuine integral

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞), for all r ≥ 0

nodes.title: r f̄(r) = ∫₀^r f for all r ≥ 0, including r = 0

edges.rationale: case r = 0: both sides vanish (0 · f(0) = 0 = ∫₀^0 f)
case r > 0: multiply (3.7) by r
case r = 0: 0 · f̄(0) = 0 = ∫₀^0 f, read through the centre value f̄(0) = f(0)

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞), for all r ≥ 0

nodes.title: Second identity of (3.8): ∂_r f̄ = (f − f̄)/r for r > 0

edges.rationale: the identity concerns the defined f̄
the "or" in (3.8) rewrites the first identity: f̄ agrees with (s f̄(s))/s on the neighbourhood (0,∞) of r, and (f(r)·r − r f̄(r))/r² = (f(r) − f̄(r))/r

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞) ; r > 0
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞), for all r > 0
nodes.source_conclusion: f̄ has (two-sided) derivative (f(r) − f̄(r))/r at r

nodes.title: For r > 0 the within-[0,∞) derivative of r f̄ is a two-sided derivative

edges.rationale: the first identity of (3.8) gives the within-[0,∞) derivative
[0,∞) is a neighbourhood of r > 0, so the within-derivative is a full derivative

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞); r > 0
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞), for all r > 0
nodes.source_conclusion: r ↦ r f̄(r) has two-sided derivative f(r) at r

nodes.title: Quotient rule for s ↦ (s f̄(s))/s at r > 0

edges.rationale: supplies the numerator's derivative f(r)
numerator s f̄(s), denominator s with derivative 1 and value r ≠ 0

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞); r > 0
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞), for all r > 0
nodes.source_conclusion: s ↦ (s·f̄(s))/s has derivative (f(r)·r − r f̄(r)·1)/r² at r

nodes.title: (3.9)-type characterization: ∂_r(rφ) = f on [0,∞) implies φ = f̄

edges.rationale: the conclusion compares φ with the defined f̄
the r > 0 case of φ = f̄
the r = 0 case of φ = f̄

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞); φ continuous on [0,∞) ; for every r in [0,∞), r ↦ rφ(r) has derivative f(r) at r within [0,∞), one-sided at r = 0 ((3.6) with h replaced by a general f, per /)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f and φ on [0,∞) such that the derivative hypothesis holds for all r ≥ 0; conclusion for all r ≥ 0
nodes.source_conclusion: φ(r) = f̄(r) for every r in [0,∞) (as functions, φ = f̄); (3.9) φ = h̄ is the instance f = h

nodes.title: φ(0) = f̄(0) by continuity of φ and f̄

edges.rationale: f̄ is continuous at 0 (φ is continuous by hypothesis)
two functions continuous at 0 that agree on (0,∞) agree at 0

nodes.source_hypotheses: f, φ continuous on [0,∞); for all r ≥ 0, r ↦ rφ(r) has derivative f(r) within [0,∞)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f and φ satisfying the hypothesis

nodes.title: φ(r) = f̄(r) for every r > 0

edges.rationale: cancel r ≠ 0 in rφ(r) = r f̄(r)

nodes.source_hypotheses: f, φ continuous on [0,∞); for all r ≥ 0, r ↦ rφ(r) has derivative f(r) within [0,∞)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f and φ satisfying the hypothesis, for all r > 0

nodes.title: rφ(r) = r f̄(r) on [0,∞) by uniqueness of antiderivatives

edges.rationale: "Thus": r f̄ has the same within-[0,∞) derivative f as rφ
two functions on [0,∞) with equal within-derivatives and equal at 0 (both 0) are equal

nodes.source_hypotheses: f, φ continuous on [0,∞); for all r ≥ 0, r ↦ rφ(r) has derivative f(r) within [0,∞)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f and φ satisfying the hypothesis, for all r ≥ 0

nodes.title: Centre value f̄(0) = f(0)

edges.rationale: under the value at r = 0 is the centre branch of the defined f̄

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞) (, ; the source requires continuity in r at r = 0)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞)
nodes.source_conclusion: f̄(0) = f(0) (the value part of [f − f̄]_{r=0} = 0 under ; the limit content is carried by n0015)

nodes.title: Continuity of f̄ on [0,∞), including the centre

edges.rationale: the claim is about the defined function f̄
case r > 0 of the pointwise continuity case split
case r = 0, which is the content of [f − f̄]_{r=0} = 0

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞) (, ; the source requires continuity in r at r = 0)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞)
nodes.source_conclusion: f̄ is continuous on [0,∞); in particular f̄(r) → f(0) as r → 0⁺ (reconstructed from [f − f̄]_{r=0} = 0)

nodes.title: Centre estimate: |f − f(0)| ≤ M on [0,r] implies |f̄(r) − f(0)| ≤ M

edges.rationale: write f̄(r) − f(0) = r⁻¹ ∫₀^r (f(s) − f(0)) ds
f is integrable on [0,r], hence so is f − f(0) (the constant f(0) is integrable)
the absolute value of ∫₀^r (f(s) − f(0)) ds is at most M·r; then divide by r

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞); r > 0; |f(s) − f(0)| ≤ M for all s ∈ [0,r]
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞), for all r > 0, for all real M

nodes.title: f̄ is continuous at every r > 0

edges.rationale: f̄ = r⁻¹ ∫₀^r f on a neighbourhood (0,∞) of r
r ↦ ∫₀^r f is differentiable hence continuous; the quotient by r ≠ 0 is continuous

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞); r > 0
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞), for all r > 0

nodes.title: f̄(r) → f(0) = f̄(0) as r → 0⁺, so f̄ is continuous at 0

edges.rationale: given ε > 0, continuity of f at 0 gives δ > 0 with abs(f(s) − f(0)) ≤ ε on [0,δ); the estimate with M = ε gives abs(f̄(r) − f(0)) ≤ ε for 0 < r < δ
the limit f(0) equals the value f̄(0)

nodes.source_hypotheses: f continuous on [0,∞) (the source requires only continuity at r = 0)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all continuous f on [0,∞)

nodes.title: Fundamental theorem of calculus for a continuous integrand
nodes.source_hypotheses: g integrable on bounded subintervals of [0,∞) and continuous at r (within [0,∞))
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all g, for all r ≥ 0
nodes.source_conclusion: s ↦ ∫₀^s g has derivative g(r) at r within [0,∞) (right derivative at r = 0)

nodes.title: Uniqueness of antiderivatives on [0,∞)
nodes.source_hypotheses: F, H : [0,∞) → ℝ; at every r ≥ 0, F and H have the same derivative within [0,∞); F(0) = H(0)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all F, H

nodes.title: Continuous functions are integrable on compact intervals
nodes.source_hypotheses: g continuous on [a,b]
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all a ≤ b, for all g

nodes.title: Sup bound for an integral
nodes.source_hypotheses: g integrable on [a,b]; |g| ≤ M on [a,b]
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all a ≤ b, for all g, for all M

nodes.title: Within-derivative at an interior point is a full derivative
nodes.source_hypotheses: F has derivative L at x within a set S; S is a neighbourhood of x
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all F, S, x, L
nodes.source_conclusion: F has (two-sided) derivative L at x

nodes.title: Continuous functions agreeing on (0,∞) agree at 0
nodes.source_hypotheses: F, H : [0,∞) → ℝ continuous at 0; F = H on (0,∞)
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all F, H

nodes.title: Quotient rule for derivatives
nodes.source_hypotheses: F has derivative a at x; H has derivative b at x; H(x) ≠ 0
nodes.source_quantifiers: for all F, H, x, a, b
nodes.source_conclusion: F/H has derivative (a H(x) − F(x) b)/H(x)² at x

coverage.reason: (3.6) h = ∂_r(rφ) enters as the derivative hypothesis of the (3.9)-type anchor, with h generalized to a continuous f ; no separate node since it is a theorem-local premise.
The definition (with the centre value) and the separate r > 0 formula anchor.
Split into two independent anchors per (first identity one-sided at 0, second only for r > 0, ); proof steps n0005, #integral-hasDerivWithinAt, #mul-mean-eq-integral, n0008, #quotient-rule.
General (3.9)-type characterization anchor ; (3.9) itself is the instance f = h. Proof steps n0013, #eq-on-pos, #eq-at-zero.

"[f − f̄]_{r=0} = 0 for f continuous at r = 0" split per into the definitional centre value and the reconstructed continuity of f̄ (which carries the limit content); proof steps n0017, #centre-estimate, #continuous-at-zero.

The coordinate domain 0 ≤ r < ∞ fixes the carrier [0,∞) for a fixed-u slice ; it enters through the domain of the defined mean and hence every anchor. Recorded as a convention (header CONVENTIONS), not as a standing-assumption node. Time is fixed for this radial-mean graph.

The evolution law D h̄ = ξ/(2r) belongs to Sect. 4 and lies outside this radial-mean graph. It uses D, ḡ, equation (3.13) and centre regularity. This graph uses only the accompanying remark that f − f̄ vanishes at the centre; Dr = −½ḡ and the centre-regularity assumption belong to the excluded evolution-law derivation.
